references.text: Laban acknowledges that he has been blessed because of Jacob, in a similar way to how the Egyptian household was blessed because of Joseph.
The Lord was with Joseph so that everything he did succeeded, and his master saw that the Lord was with him – this is the background for why God blessed the entire Egyptian household.
God's promise to Abraham that through him all families of the earth would be blessed is partially fulfilled through Joseph, who brings God's blessing to the Egyptian household.
The righteous are like a tree planted by streams of water – God's blessing follows the righteous, just as it followed Joseph and blessed everything around him.
The blessing that follows those who fear the Lord, parallel to how Joseph brought blessing to the Egyptian household.
The Lord's blessing makes rich, and toil adds nothing – this is reflected in how the Lord's blessing came upon all that Potiphar owned because of Joseph.
Both verses illustrate the biblical principle that God's presence brings blessing over the entire sphere of family and property.
Continues the same narrative thread and confirms that the Lord's presence followed Joseph regardless of whether he was free or a prisoner.
Summarizes and confirms the event in Genesis 39:5 by showing that Joseph's rule over Pharaoh's house was part of God's plan of salvation.
A direct parallel showing that God's presence (whether through the ark or a person) always brings blessing over the whole household.
